s0101.literal: He had a collected works in twenty scrolls.
s0101.idiomatic: He left collected works in twenty scrolls.

s0102.literal: Fu Zai, styled Yishi, was a man of Lingzhou in Beidi.
s0102.idiomatic: Fu Zai, styled Yishi, was from Lingzhou in Beidi.

s0103.literal: His father Yi was Liang's magistrate of Linyi.
s0103.idiomatic: His father Yi was Liang's magistrate of Linyi.

s0104.literal: Zai was clever as a child; at seven he could recite ancient poems and rhapsodies to more than a hundred thousand words.
s0104.idiomatic: Zai was clever as a child; at seven he could recite ancient poems and rhapsodies totaling more than a hundred thousand words.

s0105.literal: When grown he loved learning and could compose literature.
s0105.idiomatic: When grown he loved learning and could compose literature.

s0106.literal: At the end of Liang's Taiqing era he fled south with his mother to escape disaster; soon he suffered his mother's mourning; amid martial chaos he observed mourning rites fully, wasting away to skin and bone, and scholars praised him for this.
s0106.idiomatic: At the end of Liang's Taiqing era he fled south with his mother; soon his mother died. Amid the chaos of war he observed mourning rites fully and wasted to skin and bone, and scholars praised him for it.

s0107.literal: Later he relied on Xiao Xun, inspector of Xiangzhou; Xun greatly favored scholars and broadly gathered canonical writings; Zai indulged his will in seeking and reading and thus mastered all books.
s0107.idiomatic: Later he relied on Xiao Xun, inspector of Xiangzhou. Xun favored scholars and gathered many books; Zai read at will and came to master all fields of learning.

s0108.literal: Wang Lin heard his fame and brought him in as recorder of the staff.
s0108.idiomatic: Wang Lin heard his fame and made him recorder of the staff.

s0109.literal: When Lin was defeated, he followed Lin's general Sun Chang back to the capital.
s0109.idiomatic: When Lin was defeated, he followed Lin's general Sun Chang back to the capital.

s0110.literal: At that time Emperor Wu sent Yan Huang to present Sun Chang with various goods; Chang entrusted Zai to draft the letter of thanks; the reasoning was excellent and fluent and the text needed no correction; when Huang returned he reported this to Emperor Wu, and soon Zai was summoned as compiler-historian.
s0110.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Wu sent Yan Huang to present Sun Chang with gifts. Chang had Zai draft the letter of thanks; the reasoning was excellent and the text needed no correction. Huang reported this to Emperor Wu, and Zai was soon summoned as compiler-historian.

s0111.literal: He was appointed recorder of the staff in the bureau of the Minister of Works, then transferred to central recorder for Prince Ancheng of the Pacer Cavalry, compiling history as before.
s0111.idiomatic: He was made recorder in the bureau of the minister of works, then central recorder for Prince Ancheng of the pacer cavalry, still compiling history.

s0112.literal: Zai devoutly believed in Buddhism; from Master Huilang of Xinghuang he received the Three Treatises, [3] and fully penetrated that learning.
s0112.idiomatic: Zai was a devout Buddhist. He received the Three Treatises from Master Huilang of Xinghuang [3] and fully mastered the school.

s0113.literal: At that time the monk Daxin Hao wrote the Treatise on Non-Contention to attack him; Zai thereupon wrote the Treatise on Illuminating the Way to explain the difficulties.
s0113.idiomatic: At that time the monk Daxin Hao wrote the Treatise on Non-Contention to attack him; Zai answered with the Treatise on Illuminating the Way to resolve the objections.

s0115.literal: The Treatise on Non-Contention says: Recently there are those who promote the Three Treatises, echoing one another in reviling and slander, freely speaking charges, successively destroying all masters, rejecting and expelling the many schools, talking of the middle way yet holding a biased mind, speaking of forgetting cares yet competing to be uniquely victorious; just learning several treatises they become each other's foes; once foes are joined, great disputing arises; with such a mind they form karmic offenses; offenses unceasing—will they not again add to birth and death and the great gathering of suffering?
s0115.idiomatic: The Treatise on Non-Contention says: Lately those who promote the Three Treatises echo one another in reviling and slander, freely speak charges, destroy master after master, and reject the many schools. They talk of the middle way yet hold a biased mind; they speak of forgetting cares yet compete to win alone. Learning several treatises, they become each other's foes; once foes are joined, great disputing arises. With such a mind they form karmic offenses; offenses unceasing—will they not heap up birth, death, and great suffering?

s0116.literal: The reply says: The rise of the Three Treatises has been long.
s0116.idiomatic: The reply says: The rise of the Three Treatises has been long.

s0117.literal: Nagarjuna founded its source, removing the biased views of inner learning;
s0117.idiomatic: Nagarjuna founded its source, removing the biased views of inner learning;

s0118.literal: Deva spread its aim, sweeping away the heterodox clinging of outer paths.
s0118.idiomatic: Deva spread its aim, sweeping away the heterodox clinging of outer paths.

s0119.literal: They wished to make the great teaching flow without obstruction and the mysterious wind be opened without falling.
s0119.idiomatic: They wished the great teaching to flow without obstruction and the mysterious wind to spread without falling.

s0120.literal: Its words are vast, its meaning far, its way broad, its current deep.
s0120.idiomatic: Its words are vast, its meaning far, its way broad, its current deep.

s0121.literal: This is truly the soaring of dragon and elephant, the whirl of kun and peng.
s0121.idiomatic: This is truly the soaring of dragon and elephant, the whirl of kun and peng.

s0123.literal: [lame] riding sky-plumes, [4] how can one strain to peer into that interval?
s0123.idiomatic: [Lame] riding sky-plumes, [4] how can one strain to peer into that interval?

s0124.literal: In recent generations customs are shallow and thin; the age lacks broad-minded scholars; they merely learn petty doctrines to transform dull minds; gradual dyeing becomes custom and they lose the right road; they only compete in forced interpretations, each freely fabricating; branches and leaves grow vainly while the root source is daily obscured; one master's explanation again differs from another's; they change the old school and each sets up a new intent; among fellow students they wake and part again; thus turning and turning, admixture multiplies ever more.
s0124.idiomatic: Recent generations are shallow; the age lacks broad-minded scholars. Men learn petty doctrines to dull their minds; custom takes hold and they lose the right road. They compete in forced interpretations and each fabricates freely; branches multiply while the root is obscured. One master's explanation differs from another's; they change the old school and each sets up a new intent; fellow students wake and part again—turning thus, admixture multiplies.

s0125.literal: Taking it all together to use, the mind has no mark to aim at;
s0125.idiomatic: Taken all together, the mind has no mark to aim at;

s0126.literal: choosing what to practice, which is correct?
s0126.idiomatic: choosing what to practice, which is correct?

s0127.literal: Is this not wounding the undifferentiated by piercing it and harming the fine tree by breaking its shoots?
s0127.idiomatic: Is this not wounding the undifferentiated by piercing it and harming the fine tree by breaking its shoots?

s0128.literal: Though again men speak of the non-horse and households grasp the spirit serpent, it is like a measureless cup or a cake drawn on the ground.
s0128.idiomatic: Though men speak of the non-horse and households grasp the spirit serpent, it is like a measureless cup or a cake drawn on the ground.

s0129.literal: For losing the Way, is it not fitting?
s0129.idiomatic: For losing the Way, is it not fitting?

s0130.literal: The learning of She Mountain is not like this.
s0130.idiomatic: The learning of She Mountain is not like this.

s0131.literal: It keeps to one and follows the root, without the fault of altering and making anew;
s0131.idiomatic: It keeps to one and follows the root, without altering and making anew;

s0132.literal: it contracts the text to express the meaning and blocks the mood of arbitrary judgment.
s0132.idiomatic: it contracts the text to express the meaning and blocks arbitrary judgment.

s0133.literal: Words are not pre-spoken; principle is not long composed.
s0133.idiomatic: Words are not pre-spoken; principle is not long composed.

s0134.literal: Seeing conditions, then one responds; seeing an opponent, then one moves.
s0134.idiomatic: Seeing conditions, one responds; seeing an opponent, one moves.

s0135.literal: Vertically and horizontally they weave like post relays, suddenly dim and remote.
s0135.idiomatic: Vertically and horizontally they weave like post relays, suddenly dim and remote.

s0136.literal: Sometimes they extend the net without end, sometimes they dissolve and have no place.
s0136.idiomatic: Sometimes they extend the net without end, sometimes they dissolve and have no place.

s0137.literal: Brilliant, there is pattern; tracks and traces cannot be obtained;
s0137.idiomatic: Brilliant in pattern; tracks and traces cannot be obtained;

s0138.literal: deep, it cannot be measured—present in the affair yet not far.
s0138.idiomatic: deep beyond measure—present in the affair yet not far.

s0139.literal: Whenever they answer one another, they follow principle and examine in detail.
s0139.idiomatic: Whenever they answer one another, they follow principle and examine in detail.

s0140.literal: What jealousy and deceit is there in offending the various masters?
s0140.idiomatic: What jealousy or deceit is there in offending the various masters?

s0141.literal: Moreover, what the various masters said—can it be destroyed?
s0141.idiomatic: Moreover, can what the various masters said be destroyed?

s0142.literal: Or can it not be destroyed?
s0142.idiomatic: Or can it not be destroyed?

s0143.literal: If it can be destroyed, destruction therefore is decline;
s0143.idiomatic: If it can be destroyed, destruction is decline;

s0144.literal: if it cannot be destroyed, destruction itself does not reach it.
s0144.idiomatic: if it cannot be destroyed, destruction does not reach it.

s0145.literal: Why does the Master alone shield and protect and not allow destruction?
s0145.idiomatic: Why does the master alone shield and forbid destruction?

s0146.literal: Moreover teaching has great and small, fully set forth in the sage's instructions; the texts of the Great Vehicle then point and reproach the small path.
s0146.idiomatic: Teaching has great and small, fully set forth in the sage's instructions; the Great Vehicle texts reproach the small path.

s0147.literal: Now in promoting the great teaching, can one fail to speak the intent of the Great Vehicle?
s0147.idiomatic: Now in promoting the great teaching, can one fail to speak the intent of the Great Vehicle?

s0148.literal: Then praise and blame follow from broad promotion of learning;
s0148.idiomatic: Then praise and blame follow from broad promotion of learning;

s0149.literal: words of granting and taking away rely on the sutras for discussion.
s0149.idiomatic: words of granting and taking away rely on the sutras for discussion.

s0150.literal: How can one see the Buddha's words and believe and follow, yet in my words be contrary and rebellious?
s0150.idiomatic: How can one believe and follow the Buddha's words yet be contrary and rebellious to mine?

s0151.literal: Is this the equal mind of non-contention?
s0151.idiomatic: Is this the equal mind of non-contention?

s0152.literal: Moreover anger and affliction are the constant nature of ordinary men; those who lose principle mostly all have this.
s0152.idiomatic: Anger and affliction are the constant nature of ordinary men; those who lose principle mostly have this.

s0153.literal: How can one, because the three cultivations are not satisfied and the six masters harbor resentment, store the wonderful dharma of nirvana and never proclaim it?
s0153.idiomatic: How can one, because the three cultivations are not satisfied and the six masters harbor resentment, store the wonderful dharma of nirvana and never proclaim it?

s0154.literal: One only hopes that when the mind of anger and resentment has reached its limit, the awakening of calm detachment will form of itself.
s0154.idiomatic: One only hopes that when anger and resentment reach their limit, calm detachment will form of itself.

s0155.literal: Human faces differ and their hearts also differ; some have words and intent opposed, some have heart and mouth agreeing.
s0155.idiomatic: Faces differ and hearts differ; some speak one way and mean another, some heart and mouth agree.

s0156.literal: How can one insist that when others speak the middle way their minds are biased and clinging, while one's own practice is non-contention, outwardly not violating yet inwardly equal?
s0156.idiomatic: How can one insist that when others speak the middle way their minds are biased, while one's own practice is non-contention—outwardly compliant yet inwardly equal?

s0157.literal: Foes' quarrels and lawsuits—how is that my affair?
s0157.idiomatic: Foes' quarrels and lawsuits—how is that my affair?

s0158.literal: The gathering of karmic offenses is what disputants fear.
s0158.idiomatic: The gathering of karmic offenses is what disputants fear.

s0159.literal: The Treatise on Non-Contention says: The great master of She Mountain in enticing, advancing, transforming, and guiding is not like this—he is one who practiced and walked in non-contention.
s0159.idiomatic: The Treatise on Non-Contention says: The great master of She Mountain in enticing, advancing, transforming, and guiding was not like this—he practiced non-contention.

s0160.literal: The virtue of guiding and awakening is past; the wind of pure unity is already diluted; the mind competing for victory and the tune of reviling and destroying flourish in this age.
s0160.idiomatic: The virtue of guiding and awakening is past; the wind of pure unity is diluted; the mind of competing for victory and the tune of reviling flourish now.

s0161.literal: I wish to rest contention to open the Way and yield victory to forget virtue.
s0161.idiomatic: I wish to rest contention to open the Way and yield victory to forget virtue.

s0162.literal: Why must one exclude and brush away other schools and breed their anger?
s0162.idiomatic: Why must one exclude other schools and breed their anger?

s0163.literal: If with the mind of the middle way one practices the Chengshi, one also can be without contention;
s0163.idiomatic: If with the mind of the middle way one practices the Chengshi, one also can be without contention;

s0164.literal: if with a biased, clinging mind one speaks the Middle Treatises, one also may have contention.
s0164.idiomatic: if with a biased, clinging mind one speaks the Middle Treatises, one also may have contention.

s0165.literal: One therefore knows that contention and non-contention depend on a single dharma.
s0165.idiomatic: One therefore knows that contention and non-contention depend on a single dharma.

s0166.literal: The reply says: The great master of She Mountain was truly without contention, but what the Master prizes does not hit his measure.
s0166.idiomatic: The reply says: The great master of She Mountain was truly without contention, but what the master prizes does not hit his measure.

s0167.literal: He quietly kept to a secluded valley, silent and without acting; whenever there was instruction, none were not of one mind; in ease of speech or silence nothing was out of place—therefore though his meaning was deep, his words were very few.
s0167.idiomatic: He quietly kept to a secluded valley, silent and without acting; all who were instructed were of one mind; in speech or silence nothing was out of place—though his meaning was deep, his words were few.

s0168.literal: Today's spreading and exposition—the terrain is not so.
s0168.idiomatic: Today's spreading and exposition—the terrain is not so.

s0169.literal: Dwelling in a corner of the royal city, living within a settlement, guests who breathe and look about, men whose lips and tongues run crosswise—they sharpen points and edges, stir wings, open eyes wide and bare their courage, don armor and grasp sharp weapons, gallop other schools, display separate explanations, peep and watch for gaps, invite and hope for strengths and weaknesses, answer one another and wrestle their weight—how can one silently say nothing and only yes-yes obey orders?
s0169.idiomatic: Dwelling in a corner of the royal city, living within a settlement, guests who breathe and look about, men whose lips run crosswise—they sharpen points, stir wings, open eyes and bare courage, don armor and grasp weapons, gallop other schools, display separate explanations, watch for gaps, invite comparison, answer and wrestle for weight—how can one stay silent and only yes-yes obey?

s0170.literal: One must pick out sameness and difference, expose flaws, forget the body to spread the Way and go against custom to penetrate teaching; to take this as illness shows one knows one has not attained.
s0170.idiomatic: One must pick out sameness and difference, expose flaws, forget the body to spread the Way and go against custom to penetrate teaching; to take this as illness shows one has not attained.

s0171.literal: If the great master were in this place, why must he silence himself yet be prized by the Master?
s0171.idiomatic: If the great master were in this place, why must he silence himself yet be prized by the master?

s0172.literal: The Master also said: "I wish to rest contention to open the Way and yield victory to forget virtue.
s0172.idiomatic: The master also said, "I wish to rest contention to open the Way and yield victory to forget virtue.

s0173.literal: " Matters of virtue and the Way are not only in contending or not contending, yielding or not yielding.
s0173.idiomatic: " Matters of virtue and the Way are not only in contending or not contending, yielding or not yielding.

s0174.literal: This saying is simply what the human world esteems; the Master admires it and speaks it, yet in the end does not know how victory can be yielded.
s0174.idiomatic: This saying is simply what the world esteems; the master admires it and speaks it, yet does not know how victory can be yielded.

s0175.literal: If another's Way is high, then victory of itself needs no yielding;
s0175.idiomatic: If another's Way is high, victory needs no yielding;

s0176.literal: if another's Way is low, then though one yields it is of no benefit.
s0176.idiomatic: if another's Way is low, yielding brings no benefit.

s0177.literal: Words of wishing to yield—are they not empty setup?
s0177.idiomatic: Words of wishing to yield—are they not empty setup?

s0178.literal: The mind of the middle way has no place where it cannot be.
s0178.idiomatic: The mind of the middle way has no place where it cannot be.

s0179.literal: Chengshi and Three Treatises—what matter makes them diverge?
s0179.idiomatic: Chengshi and Three Treatises—what makes them diverge?

s0180.literal: One need only rest the interpretation of guarding a stump and remove the intent of gluing the peg; in these matters all are centered.
s0180.idiomatic: One need only rest the interpretation of guarding a stump and remove the intent of gluing the peg; in these matters all are centered.

s0181.literal: Your message says "contention and non-contention depend on a single dharma."
s0181.idiomatic: Your message says "contention and non-contention depend on a single dharma."

s0183.literal: Is this not spear and shield?
s0183.idiomatic: Is this not spear and shield?

s0184.literal: The Treatise on Non-Contention says: Wrong and right, gain and loss, victory and defeat, and is and is-not must arise in the mind; it is not that the dharma spoken has a fixed mark by which to discuss superiority and inferiority.
s0184.idiomatic: The Treatise on Non-Contention says: Wrong and right, gain and loss, victory and defeat must arise in the mind; the dharma spoken has no fixed mark for judging superiority.

s0185.literal: If in different treatises on is and is-not one takes biased clinging as faulty speech, and no-is and no-is-not dissolve gain and loss, and with this treatise as supremely victorious beyond what other treatises reach—this also is fault.
s0185.idiomatic: If one takes biased clinging as faulty, dissolves gain and loss in no-is and no-is-not, and holds this treatise supreme beyond others—that also is fault.

s0187.literal: Whatever the mind destroys, is there not a mind in the one who can destroy? Then the mind of victory and defeat is not forgotten—will it not still harbor the victor?
s0187.idiomatic: Whatever the mind destroys, is there not a mind in the destroyer? Then the mind of victory and defeat is not forgotten—does it not still harbor the victor?

s0188.literal: Then one prides oneself as having got it and abandons another's fault; thereupon is taking and rejecting, greatly producing is and is-not—this is increasing contention.
s0188.idiomatic: Then one prides oneself as right and abandons another's fault; taking and rejecting arise and is and is-not grow—this increases contention.

s0189.literal: The reply says: Words are the mind's envoy; the mind receives words' explication;
s0189.idiomatic: The reply says: Words are the mind's envoy; the mind receives words' explication;

s0190.literal: joining roots and dust, stirring wind and qi, therefore words are formed.
s0190.idiomatic: joining roots and dust, stirring wind and qi, therefore words are formed.

s0191.literal: Affairs must come from the mind, as the Tathagata said.
s0191.idiomatic: Affairs must come from the mind, as the Tathagata said.

s0192.literal: As for the mind making falsity to employ the mouth and the mouth practicing deceit to answer the mind, outwardly harmonious yet inwardly dangerous, words following yet intent opposing, seeking profit and support and drawing fame—those who enter the Way and gentlemen at home, such are not one.
s0192.idiomatic: The mind may make falsity to employ the mouth and the mouth practice deceit to answer the mind—outwardly harmonious yet inwardly dangerous, words following yet intent opposing, seeking profit and fame. Those who enter the Way and gentlemen at home—such are not few.

s0193.literal: The sage therefore bent his teaching and deeply set up guards and blocks, speaking present calamities and guilt and narrating coming miseries and harms; this pattern is bright and clear, more than sun and moon—yet there are those who forget love of body, brave stern prohibition, tread boiling coals and sweeten chaff powder, certain to act and not look back.
s0193.idiomatic: The sage therefore bent his teaching and set up guards, speaking present calamities and future harms; this is brighter than sun and moon—yet some forget love of body, brave stern prohibition, tread boiling coals and sweeten chaff powder, and act without looking back.

s0194.literal: How can they be pleased by compositions on non-contention and turn their heads to change their tune?
s0194.idiomatic: How can they be pleased by compositions on non-contention and turn to change their tune?

s0195.literal: If men who spread the Way and gentlemen who proclaim transformation know in mind they are victorious and in mouth speak victory, know in mind they are inferior and in mouth speak inferiority, they also have nothing hidden and nothing feared—they only act with a straight mind.
s0195.idiomatic: If those who spread the Way know in mind they are victorious and speak victory, know they are inferior and speak inferiority, they hide nothing and fear nothing—they only act with a straight mind.

s0196.literal: Another's Way though inferior is still the sage's teaching;
s0196.idiomatic: Another's Way though inferior is still the sage's teaching;

s0197.literal: one's own virtue though superior is also the sage's teaching.
s0197.idiomatic: one's own virtue though superior is also the sage's teaching.

s0198.literal: If I am victorious then the sage is victorious; if another is inferior then the sage is inferior.
s0198.idiomatic: If I am victorious the sage is victorious; if another is inferior the sage is inferior.

s0199.literal: The sage's superiority and inferiority are probably what roots and conditions make fitting.
s0199.idiomatic: The sage's superiority and inferiority are probably what roots and conditions make fitting.

s0200.literal: Regarding that and this, what partiality or thickness is there?
s0200.idiomatic: Regarding that and this, what partiality is there?
